paper_title: Gas-rich dwarf galaxies as a new probe of dark matter interactions with ordinary matter
notes: Paper derives constraints on ultra-light hidden photon dark matter (HPDM) using observations of the Leo T dwarf galaxy. The constraint is based on requiring that DM-gas heating via kinetic mixing does not exceed the ultra-low radiative cooling rate of neutral hydrogen gas in Leo T's inner region (r < 0.35 kpc). The paper reports that Leo T constraints are stronger than all previous literature for the mass range 10^-23 ≲ m_DM ≲ 10^-10 eV. Data points extracted from Fig. 2 (black curve, Leo T bounds). The coupling parameter g is the dimensionless kinetic mixing strength between hidden photons and standard model photons. The paper also constrains millicharged DM and general DM-baryon interactions, but the primary novel result is on HPDM. No local DM density assumption is needed for this astrophysical heating constraint (unlike direct detection experiments). Confidence is high for the HPDM coupling type identification, though exact numerical values from the figure are approximate due to plot resolution. | selector: text (sole candidate)
